sourceHtml:
Organizations building AI agents face a common challenge: Every request, whether a routine status check or complex analysis, typically gets routed to a single large, expensive model. This one-size-fits-all approach can drive up API costs, introduce unpredictable latency, and remove the possibility of offline operation. Even routine queries that could resolve locally end up requiring a full network round-trip to a cloud-hosted large language model (LLM).

The Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework (AAIF), built with Strands Agents, takes a different approach. Instead of routing all requests to a single large model, AAIF uses small language models (SLMs) to handle routine tasks locally. More complex requests are routed to cloud-hosted models through Amazon Bedrock. This approach builds on the research position from Belcak et al. at NVIDIA. They argue that small language models are “sufficiently powerful, inherently more suitable, and necessarily more economical for many invocations in agentic systems.” Built on Strands Agents, the framework demonstrates how intelligent model orchestration can help reduce costs while maintaining low latency for local operations.

In this post, we walk through the key components of AAIF using Strands Agents with local SLMs through Ollama and cloud models through Amazon Bedrock. We use an Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring scenario as a reference implementation.

Solution overview

AAIF organizes AI processing into three layers, each optimized for different task types, as Figure 1 shows:

  1. Smart orchestration uses a lightweight SLM (llama3.2:1b) as the decision-making layer. This orchestrator classifies incoming requests and routes them to the appropriate processing layer without hardcoded rules.
  2. Local processing handles routine tasks like device telemetry retrieval and image analysis using SLMs running on local hardware through Ollama. These tasks complete with low latency and no cloud dependency.
  3. Cloud processing handles complex pattern analysis and strategic recommendations through frontier models in Amazon Bedrock. These requests need broader context and multi-step reasoning that SLMs cannot reliably provide.

Figure 1: The three AAIF processing layers for smart orchestration, local processing, and cloud processing

Figure 1 shows the complete AAIF system architecture. At the center sits the Strands agent, which connects to an Ollama runtime hosting both the 1B-parameter orchestrator model and the vision model. The agent exposes three tools: get_device_telemetry for local sensor data retrieval, analyze_camera_feed for on-device vision processing through llama3.2-vision, and get_expert_insights which calls Amazon Bedrock through boto3 for complex analysis. Incoming user requests flow through the SLM orchestrator, which classifies each request and dispatches it to either a local tool or the cloud endpoint based on task complexity.

Figure 2: Complete AAIF system architecture showing the Strands agent, Ollama runtime, tool integrations, and Amazon Bedrock connectivity

The framework adapts to your deployment constraints rather than requiring you to restructure your infrastructure around it. This architecture runs on edge devices like a Raspberry Pi with 8 GB of memory, in full cloud deployments where all inference hits Amazon Bedrock, or in hybrid configurations that combine local speed with cloud reasoning. The flexibility comes from separating the routing logic (the SLM orchestrator) from the processing tools, which you can swap or reconfigure independently depending on available hardware and network connectivity.

Prerequisites

For this walkthrough, you should have the following prerequisites:

  • An AWS account.
  • Amazon Bedrock model access configured in the required Region.
  • Python 3.10+ installed.
  • Ollama installed with the following models pulled:
    • ollama pull llama3.2:1b (orchestrator).
    • ollama pull llama3.2-vision (vision analysis).
  • Strands Agents installed: pip install strands-agents strands-agents-tools.
  • AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) configured with appropriate credentials.
  • Boto3 installed: pip install boto3.

Set up the environment

Create a project directory and start the Ollama server:

mkdir aaif-demo && cd aaif-demo
ollama serve

Pull the required models:

ollama pull llama3.2:1b
ollama pull llama3.2-vision

Create a file called aaif_agent.py and add the following components.

Implement local processing tools

Strands Agents uses the @tool decorator to define capabilities that agents can invoke. Start by creating tools for local processing.

The first tool retrieves device telemetry data. In a production environment, this would connect to actual IoT sensors. For this walkthrough, it uses simulated device data:

from strands import Agent, tool
import random

DEVICE_TELEMETRY = {
    "sensor-001": {
        "device_type": "Temperature Sensor",
        "location": "Building A - Floor 2",
        "temperature": 72.5,
        "humidity": 45.2,
        "status": "normal"
    },
    "camera-001": {
        "device_type": "Security Camera",
        "location": "Main Entrance",
        "fps": 30,
        "resolution": "1080p",
        "status": "recording"
    },
    "hvac-001": {
        "device_type": "HVAC Controller",
        "location": "Building A - Central",
        "set_temp": 71.0,
        "current_temp": 72.5,
        "mode": "cooling",
        "status": "active"
    }
}

@tool
def get_device_telemetry() -> str:
    """Retrieve current telemetry data from connected IoT devices."""
    device_id = random.choice(list(DEVICE_TELEMETRY.keys()))
    device_data = DEVICE_TELEMETRY[device_id]

    report = f"Device: {device_id} ({device_data['device_type']})\n"
    report += f"Location: {device_data['location']}\n"
    report += f"Status: {device_data['status']}\n"
    for key, value in device_data.items():
        if key not in ['device_type', 'location', 'status']:
            report += f"{key}: {value}\n"
    return report

The second tool performs vision analysis using a local SLM. The llama3.2-vision model runs entirely on local hardware, which means sensitive camera feeds don’t leave the device:

import ollama

@tool
def analyze_camera_feed(image_path: str) -> str:
    """Analyze visual data from cameras using local vision model."""
    stream = ollama.chat(
        model='llama3.2-vision',
        messages=[{
            'role': 'user',
            'content': 'Describe this image in one sentence. '
            'What are the 3 most important things you see?',
            'images': [image_path]
        }],
        stream=True,
    )

    full_response = ""
    for chunk in stream:
        chunk_content = chunk['message']['content']
        print(chunk_content, end='', flush=True)
        full_response += chunk_content

    return f"Object Detection Report:\n{full_response}"

Implement cloud processing

For complex analysis that requires broader reasoning, create a tool that calls Amazon Bedrock. This tool is invoked only when the orchestrator determines that local models can’t handle the request:

import boto3

@tool
def get_expert_insights(context_data: str, question: str) -> str:
    """Get advanced analysis and expert recommendations
    for complex questions via Amazon Bedrock."""
    client = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1")

    conversation = [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"text": f"Context: {context_data}\n\nQuestion: {question}"}
            ],
        }
    ]

    response = client.converse(
        modelId="<<model_id>", //Refer model id [details](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.html)
        messages=conversation,
        inferenceConfig={
            "maxTokens": 512,
            "temperature": 0.5,
            "topP": 0.9
        }
    )

    response_text = response["output"]["message"]["content"][0]["text"]
    return f"Expert Analysis:\n{response_text}"

Configure the Strands agent with smart orchestration

The core of AAIF is the Strands agent configuration. The agent uses a local SLM (llama3.2:1b) as its orchestrator. Strands Agents supports multiple model providers, and here we use the Ollama provider to run the orchestrator locally:

from strands.models.ollama import OllamaModel

model = OllamaModel(
    model_id="llama3.2:1b",
    host="http://localhost:11434",
    params={
        "max_tokens": 300,
        "temperature": 0.3,
    },
)

system_prompt = """You are a monitoring assistant for operational facilities.
You have access to device telemetry tools, analysis capabilities,
and expert insights to help monitor operations effectively.

When users ask for:
- Device status or telemetry: use get_device_telemetry
- Image or data analysis: use analyze_camera_feed
- Expert advice or complex questions: use get_expert_insights

Always return the complete tool results directly to the user."""

agent = Agent(
    model=model,
    system_prompt=system_prompt,
    tools=[
        get_device_telemetry,
        analyze_camera_feed,
        get_expert_insights,
    ],
)

The SLM-powered orchestrator analyzes each request and routes it to the appropriate tool without hardcoded keyword matching. The routing happens through the model’s understanding of the request:

Request Routing Latency
“Check device status” Local SLM Low (local inference)
“Analyze this image” Local vision AI Low (local inference)
“What optimization strategies do you recommend?” Cloud (Amazon Bedrock) Higher (network round-trip)

Table 1: Request, routing, and latency estimates for local compared to cloud inference

Run the agent

With the agent configured, you can interact with it directly:

# Local processing - device telemetry
response = agent("What's the current status of our devices?")
print(response)

# Local processing - vision analysis
response = agent("Analyze the camera feed from camera-001")
print(response)

# Cloud processing - complex analysis
response = agent(
    "Based on current telemetry patterns, "
    "what optimization strategies do you recommend?"
)
print(response)

The agent automatically classifies each request and routes it to the appropriate processing layer. No explicit routing rules are needed.

Adapt to different deployment scenarios

The AAIF architecture adapts to different infrastructure requirements by changing the model configuration:

When your workload runs entirely in the cloud and no edge hardware is available, replace the Ollama model configuration with Amazon Bedrock for all processing. This routes every request through managed cloud inference, giving you auto scaling without requiring local GPU resources. Teams with reliable low-latency connectivity and no data residency constraints benefit most from this configuration:

from strands.models import BedrockModel

model = BedrockModel(
    model_id="<<model_id>", //Refer model id [details](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.html)
    region_name="us-east-1"
)

The hybrid configuration keeps the local SLM orchestrator intact while adding cloud models for requests that exceed local model capabilities. This is the default AAIF configuration shown in this walkthrough. It suits environments where most requests are routine enough to resolve locally, but some require the broader reasoning of a larger model. Cost savings can come from the roughly 80 percent of traffic that doesn’t hit a paid API endpoint.

For environments that are fully air-gapped or have strict data sovereignty requirements, replace the cloud tool with a larger local model and run all processing on-device. A 3B-parameter model running on hardware with adequate memory can handle moderately complex tasks that the 1B orchestrator would otherwise escalate. The trade-off is reduced reasoning depth on the hardest queries, but the benefit is data not leaving the premises:

model = OllamaModel(
    model_id="llama3.2:3b", # Larger local model for complex tasks
    host="http://localhost:11434",
)

Looking ahead: Centralized tool calling with MCP servers

The implementation in this post uses local tool calls defined directly in the agent code. For production deployments with multiple agents sharing tools across services, expose these tools as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. MCP provides a standardized interface for tool discovery and invocation, so you can centralize tool management and reuse tools across different agents and environments. In Figure 3, we show how to convert AAIF tools into MCP servers for distributed, centralized tool calling.

In the distributed configuration as shown in Figure 3, Device 1 acts as the orchestrating hub, running the Strands agent with the SLM router and a local telemetry tool. It connects through the MCP protocol to Device 2, which runs an edge vision processing server with llama3.2-vision. Device 3 serves as a cloud analytics gateway connected to Amazon Bedrock. From the orchestrator’s perspective, all remote tools appear as local function calls because the MCP transport layer handles serialization and network communication transparently.

Figure 3: Distributed intelligence with MCP servers

Cleaning up

To avoid incurring future charges, complete the following cleanup steps:

  1. Disable Amazon Bedrock model access: Open the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Model access, and revoke access for Amazon Nova Lite. For detailed steps, see Manage model access in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
  2. Stop the Ollama server and remove models to free local disk space (approximately 2 GB): 
    ollama stop
ollama rm llama3.2:1b
ollama rm llama3.2-vision
  3. Delete the project directory if you no longer need the sample code: 
    rm -rf aaif-demo

Conclusion

We showed how to build cost-effective AI agents using the Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework with Strands Agents. By routing routine requests to local SLMs and reserving cloud models on Amazon Bedrock for complex analysis, AAIF can help reduce API costs while maintaining low latency for routine operations.

Before you run this pattern in production, add responsible AI controls to the cloud inference path, since those requests carry tool outputs, retrieved data, and user input. You can attach Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to the Strands BedrockModel with a guardrail ID and version. It then applies content filters for harmful categories, prompt injection filters, and contextual grounding checks that block responses not supported by the source data. To apply the same policies to the local SLM tier, call the standalone ApplyGuardrail API on its inputs and outputs. This way, every request follows one safety standard no matter which model handles it.

This architectural pattern applies beyond IoT monitoring. A healthcare organization could run patient monitoring locally while routing diagnosis support to cloud models. A financial services firm could process transactions on-premises and reserve cloud capacity for risk analysis. A manufacturing team could run quality control vision models at the edge while sending optimization requests to the cloud.

To learn more about building agents with Strands Agents, visit the Strands Agents documentation. For information about available foundation models, see Amazon Bedrock.

About the authors

构建 AI 智能体的组织面临一个共同挑战：每个请求，无论是例行状态检查还是复杂分析，通常都会被路由到同一个规模大、成本高的模型。这种一刀切的做法可能推高 API 成本，带来难以预测的延迟，并使离线运行成为不可能。即使是本可在本地解决的常规查询，最终也需要通过网络与云端托管的大语言模型（LLM）进行一次完整的往返通信。

使用 Strands Agents 构建的自适应智能体智能框架（Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework，AAIF）采用了不同的方法。AAIF 不会将所有请求都路由到同一个大模型，而是使用小语言模型（SLM）在本地处理常规任务。更复杂的请求则会被路由到 Amazon Bedrock 上托管的云端模型。这种方法以 NVIDIA 的 Belcak 等人的研究观点为基础。他们认为，对于智能体系统中的许多调用，小语言模型“能力足够强，本质上更适合，而且必然更经济”。该框架基于 Strands Agents 构建，展示了如何通过智能模型编排降低成本，同时保持本地操作的低延迟。

本文将介绍 AAIF 的关键组件，使用 Strands Agents，通过 Ollama 调用本地 SLM，并通过 Amazon Bedrock 调用云端模型。我们以物联网（IoT）监控场景作为参考实现。

解决方案概述

AAIF 将 AI 处理划分为三个层次，每一层都针对不同任务类型进行了优化，如图 1 所示：

  1. 智能编排使用轻量级 SLM（llama3.2:1b）作为决策层。该编排器对传入请求进行分类，并将其路由到适当的处理层，无需硬编码规则。
  2. 本地处理通过 Ollama，使用在本地硬件上运行的 SLM 处理设备遥测数据检索和图像分析等常规任务。这些任务能够以低延迟完成，且不依赖云端。
  3. 云端处理通过 Amazon Bedrock 中的前沿模型执行复杂的模式分析并提供战略建议。这些请求需要更广泛的上下文和多步推理，而 SLM 无法可靠地提供这些能力。

图 1：AAIF 的三个处理层，分别用于智能编排、本地处理和云端处理

图 1 展示了完整的 AAIF 系统架构。架构中心是 Strands 智能体，它连接到一个 Ollama 运行时，该运行时同时托管具有 10 亿参数的编排器模型和视觉模型。智能体提供三个工具：get_device_telemetry，用于检索本地传感器数据；analyze_camera_feed，用于通过 llama3.2-vision 在设备上执行视觉处理；以及 get_expert_insights，用于通过 boto3 调用 Amazon Bedrock 进行复杂分析。传入的用户请求经过 SLM 编排器，由它对每个请求进行分类，并根据任务复杂程度将请求分派到本地工具或云端端点。

图 2：完整的 AAIF 系统架构，展示了 Strands 智能体、Ollama 运行时、工具集成以及与 Amazon Bedrock 的连接

该框架能够适应您的部署约束，无需您围绕它重新调整基础设施。此架构既可以运行在配备 8 GB 内存的 Raspberry Pi 等边缘设备上，也可以采用所有推理都通过 Amazon Bedrock 执行的纯云端部署，还可以采用结合本地速度与云端推理能力的混合配置。这种灵活性源于将路由逻辑（SLM 编排器）与处理工具分离，您可以根据可用硬件和网络连接情况，独立替换或重新配置这些工具。

先决条件

在开始本演练之前，您应具备以下条件：

  • 一个 AWS 账户。
  • 已在所需区域配置 Amazon Bedrock 模型访问权限。
  • 已安装 Python 3.10+。
  • Ollama installed with the following models pulled:
    • ollama pull llama3.2:1b（编排器）。
    • ollama pull llama3.2-vision（视觉分析）。
  • 已安装 Strands Agents：pip install strands-agents strands-agents-tools。
  • 已使用适当的凭证配置 AWS Command Line Interface（AWS CLI）。
  • 已安装 Boto3：pip install boto3。

设置环境

创建项目目录并启动 Ollama 服务器：

mkdir aaif-demo && cd aaif-demo
ollama serve

拉取所需模型：

ollama pull llama3.2:1b
ollama pull llama3.2-vision

创建一个名为 aaif_agent.py 的文件，并添加以下组件。

实现本地处理工具

Strands Agents 使用 @tool 装饰器定义智能体可以调用的能力。首先创建用于本地处理的工具。

第一个工具用于检索设备遥测数据。在生产环境中，它会连接实际的 IoT 传感器。在本演练中，它使用模拟设备数据：

from strands import Agent, tool
import random

DEVICE_TELEMETRY = {
    "sensor-001": {
        "device_type": "Temperature Sensor",
        "location": "Building A - Floor 2",
        "temperature": 72.5,
        "humidity": 45.2,
        "status": "normal"
    },
    "camera-001": {
        "device_type": "Security Camera",
        "location": "Main Entrance",
        "fps": 30,
        "resolution": "1080p",
        "status": "recording"
    },
    "hvac-001": {
        "device_type": "HVAC Controller",
        "location": "Building A - Central",
        "set_temp": 71.0,
        "current_temp": 72.5,

        "status": "active"
    }
}

@tool
def get_device_telemetry() -> str:

            report += f"{key}: {value}\n"
    return report

第二个工具使用本地 SLM 执行视觉分析。llama3.2-vision 模型完全在本地硬件上运行，这意味着敏感的摄像头视频流不会离开设备：

import ollama

@tool
def analyze_camera_feed(image_path: str) -> str:
    """Analyze visual data from cameras using local vision model."""
    stream = ollama.chat(

        chunk_content = chunk['message']['content']
        print(chunk_content, end='', flush=True)
        full_response += chunk_content

    return f"Object Detection Report:\n{full_response}"

实现云端处理

对于需要更广泛推理能力的复杂分析，创建一个调用 Amazon Bedrock 的工具。只有当编排器判定本地模型无法处理请求时，才会调用此工具：

import boto3

@tool
def get_expert_insights(context_data: str, question: str) -> str:
    """Get advanced analysis and expert recommendations
    for complex questions via Amazon Bedrock."""
    client = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1")

    conversation = [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"text": f"Context: {context_data}\n\nQuestion: {question}"}
            ],
        }
    ]

    response = client.converse(
        modelId="<<model_id>", //Refer model id [details](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.html)
        messages=conversation,
        inferenceConfig={
            "maxTokens": 512,
            "temperature": 0.5,
            "topP": 0.9
        }
    )

    response_text = response["output"]["message"]["content"][0]["text"]
    return f"Expert Analysis:\n{response_text}"

为 Strands 智能体配置智能编排

AAIF 的核心是 Strands 智能体的配置。该智能体使用本地 SLM（llama3.2:1b）作为编排器。Strands Agents 支持多种模型提供方，这里我们使用 Ollama 提供方在本地运行编排器：

from strands.models.ollama import OllamaModel

model = OllamaModel(
    model_id="llama3.2:1b",
    host="http://localhost:11434",
    params={
        "max_tokens": 300,
        "temperature": 0.3,
    },
)

system_prompt = """You are a monitoring assistant for operational facilities.
You have access to device telemetry tools, analysis capabilities,
and expert insights to help monitor operations effectively.

When users ask for:
- Device status or telemetry: use get_device_telemetry
- Image or data analysis: use analyze_camera_feed
- Expert advice or complex questions: use get_expert_insights

Always return the complete tool results directly to the user."""

agent = Agent(
    model=model,
    system_prompt=system_prompt,
    tools=[
        get_device_telemetry,
        analyze_camera_feed,
        get_expert_insights,
    ],
)

由 SLM 驱动的编排器会分析每个请求，并将其路由到适当的工具，无需硬编码的关键词匹配。路由依据模型对请求的理解来完成：

请求 路由 延迟
“检查设备状态” 本地 SLM 低（本地推理）
“分析这张图像” 本地视觉 AI 低（本地推理）
“您推荐哪些优化策略？” 云端（Amazon Bedrock） 较高（网络往返通信）

表 1：本地推理与云端推理的请求、路由和延迟估算对比

运行智能体

配置好智能体后，您可以直接与其交互：

# Local processing - device telemetry
response = agent("What's the current status of our devices?")
print(response)

# Local processing - vision analysis
response = agent("Analyze the camera feed from camera-001")
print(response)

# Cloud processing - complex analysis
response = agent(
    "Based on current telemetry patterns, "
    "what optimization strategies do you recommend?"
)
print(response)

智能体会自动对每个请求进行分类，并将其路由到适当的处理层。无需显式路由规则。

适应不同的部署场景

AAIF 架构通过更改模型配置来适应不同的基础设施要求：

当您的工作负载完全在云端运行且没有可用的边缘硬件时，将 Ollama 模型配置替换为 Amazon Bedrock，以执行所有处理。这样，每个请求都会通过托管式云端推理进行处理，无需本地 GPU 资源即可实现自动扩缩容。具有可靠低延迟连接且没有数据驻留限制的团队，最能从此配置中受益：

from strands.models import BedrockModel

model = BedrockModel(
    model_id="<<model_id>", //Refer model id [details](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.html)
    region_name="us-east-1"
)

混合配置保留本地 SLM 编排器，同时添加云端模型，以处理超出本地模型能力的请求。这是本演练中展示的默认 AAIF 配置。它适用于大多数请求较为常规、可在本地解决，但部分请求需要更大模型提供更广泛推理能力的环境。约 80% 的流量不会访问付费 API 端点，由此可以节省成本。

对于完全物理隔离或具有严格数据主权要求的环境，可以使用更大的本地模型替换云端工具，并在设备上执行所有处理。在内存充足的硬件上运行的 30 亿参数模型，可以处理具有 10 亿参数的编排器原本会升级交由更强模型处理的中等复杂度任务。代价是处理最困难查询时的推理深度有所降低，但好处是数据不会离开本地场所：

model = OllamaModel(
    model_id="llama3.2:3b", # Larger local model for complex tasks
    host="http://localhost:11434",
)

展望：使用 MCP 服务器实现集中式工具调用

本文的实现使用直接在智能体代码中定义的本地工具调用。对于多个智能体跨服务共享工具的生产部署，可将这些工具作为模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器对外提供。MCP 为工具发现和调用提供了标准化接口，因此您可以集中管理工具，并在不同智能体和环境中复用工具。图 3 展示了如何将 AAIF 工具转换为 MCP 服务器，以实现分布式、集中管理的工具调用。

在图 3 所示的分布式配置中，设备 1 充当编排枢纽，运行配备 SLM 路由器和本地遥测工具的 Strands 智能体。它通过 MCP 协议连接到设备 2，后者运行使用 llama3.2-vision 的边缘视觉处理服务器。设备 3 则充当连接 Amazon Bedrock 的云端分析网关。从编排器的角度看，所有远程工具都表现为本地函数调用，因为 MCP 传输层会透明地处理序列化和网络通信。

清理资源

为避免今后产生费用，请完成以下清理步骤：

  1. 禁用 Amazon Bedrock 模型访问权限：打开 Amazon Bedrock 控制台，选择 Model access，然后撤销 Amazon Nova Lite 的访问权限。详细步骤请参阅《Amazon Bedrock 用户指南》中的管理模型访问权限。
  2. Stop the Ollama server and remove models to free local disk space (approximately 2 GB):

ollama rm llama3.2:1b

结论

我们展示了如何结合自适应智能体智能框架与 Strands Agents，构建经济高效的 AI 智能体。通过将常规请求路由到本地 SLM，并将 Amazon Bedrock 上的云端模型留给复杂分析，AAIF 可以帮助降低 API 成本，同时保持常规操作的低延迟。

在生产环境中运行此模式之前，请为云端推理路径添加负责任 AI 控制措施，因为这些请求携带工具输出、检索到的数据和用户输入。您可以使用防护规则 ID 和版本，将 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 关联到 Strands BedrockModel。随后，它会应用针对有害类别的内容过滤器、提示注入过滤器，以及上下文依据检查，以阻止缺乏源数据支持的响应。若要将相同策略应用于本地 SLM 层，请对其输入和输出调用独立的 ApplyGuardrail API。这样，无论由哪个模型处理，每个请求都遵循同一套安全标准。

这种架构模式的适用范围不限于 IoT 监控。医疗机构可以在本地运行患者监护，同时将诊断支持请求路由到云端模型。金融服务公司可以在本地处理交易，并将云端容量留给风险分析。制造团队可以在边缘运行质量控制视觉模型，同时将优化请求发送到云端。

要了解有关使用 Strands Agents 构建智能体的更多信息，请访问 Strands Agents 文档。有关可用基础模型的信息，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock。
